kaps_punt: Inenting teen pokke en die rol van Edward Jenner

items.bewering: Pokke was een van die siektes waarvoor mense die bangste was.
items.blok: 'n Siekte waarvoor mense baie bang was
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox (who.int/emergencies/situations/smallpox): 'one of the most devastating diseases known to humanity and caused millions of deaths'. The softened form 'een van die' is the careful version and holds.

items.bewering: Dit was 'n aansteeklike siekte wat maklik van mens tot mens versprei het.
items.blok: 'n Siekte waarvoor mense baie bang was
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox: 'an acute contagious disease caused by the variola virus'; CDC Museum, Story of CDC: Smallpox (cdc.gov/museum/online/story-of-cdc/smallpox/): the virus is found only in humans and patients stay contagious until all scabs fall off.

items.bewering: Baie mense het aan pokke gesterf.
items.blok: 'n Siekte waarvoor mense baie bang was
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox ('caused millions of deaths'); CDC Museum, Smallpox (killed about one-third of its victims).

items.bewering: Wie dit oorleef het, het dikwels diep merke op die vel oorgehou.
items.blok: 'n Siekte waarvoor mense baie bang was
items.bron: CDC Museum, Smallpox: scabs fall away and leave pitted scars; estimates of facial scarring among survivors run around 65-80% (Wyoming Department of Health presentation). 'Dikwels' is accurate.

items.bewering: Vroue wat koeie gemelk het, het soms koeipokke gekry, 'n siekte met pynlike sere op die hande.
items.blok: Wat op die plase opgeval het
items.bron: Jenner, An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae (1798), Project Gutenberg #29414: 'Inflamed spots now begin to appear on different parts of the hands of the domestics employed in milking' ... 'ulcerated sores about the hands, which, from the sensibility of the parts, are very troublesome.' Men who milked caught it too, but the lesson says 'soms' and makes no exclusive claim.

items.bewering: Dit kon 'n vrou 'n paar dae van haar werk afhou.
items.blok: Wat op die plase opgeval het
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case VI: Sarah Wynne was 'rendered incapable for several days of pursuing her ordinary vocations in the farm'; Case I similar.

items.bewering: Mense op die plase het opgemerk dat baie van hierdie vroue daarna nie pokke kry nie. Hierdie verband was al voor Edward Jenner bekend onder mense wat met koeie gewerk het.
items.blok: Wat op die plase opgeval het
items.bron: Historical review, PMC3883152 (NIH), and History News Network (University of Richmond): the belief that dairy workers who had cowpox were protected from smallpox circulated in the 1760s; the farmer Benjamin Jesty acted on it in 1774, before Jenner. Jenner's Inquiry Case II also records a farm worker who believed herself secure after cowpox.

items.bewering: Edward Jenner was 'n dokter in Engeland en het die verband in 1796 getoets.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), title page 'Edward Jenner, M.D. F.R.S.', Berkeley, Gloucestershire; Wikipedia 'James Phipps' (citing Jenner): inoculation on 14 May 1796; WHO Smallpox: Jenner's 1796 vaccine.

items.bewering: Hy het etter uit 'n sweer van koeipokke op 'n melkmeisie se hand geneem.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case XVII: matter taken 'from a sore on the hand of a dairymaid' infected by her master's cows; the editor's note names her as Sarah Nelmes.

items.bewering: Hy het dit in twee klein snytjies in die arm van 'n seun van agt gesit.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case XVII: 'a healthy boy, about eight years old' ... 'inserted into the arm of the boy by means of two superficial incisions, barely penetrating the cutis, each about half an inch long.'

items.bewering: Die seun was James Phipps, en hy het net liggies siek geword.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case XVII: on the ninth day 'he became a little chilly, lost his appetite, and had a slight head-ach' and was well again the next day; Wikipedia 'James Phipps' names him.

items.bewering: Toe Jenner die seun later aan pokke blootstel, het James nie pokke gekry nie.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case XVII: 'inoculated the 1st of July following with variolous matter' with no effect, and again several months later with 'no sensible effect'; Nature (d42859-020-00007-6): Jenner variolated Phipps in July 1796.

items.bewering: Jenner het die proef herhaal en sy werk in 1798 gepubliseer.
items.bron: Nature (d42859-020-00007-6): after the Royal Society rejected his first report, Jenner self-published a longer monograph in 1798; the Inquiry itself records further cases (e.g. William Summers) inoculated with cowpox and then tested with smallpox.

items.bewering: Ander dokters kon dit toe self nagaan en naboots.
items.bron: Nature (381018b0) and Medical and Physical Journal reprints on PMC (PMC5650786, PMC5650836): William Woodville in London tested cowpox inoculation in 1799 using Jenner's Inquiry, with some 200 case histories; George Pearson's investigations 'tended to confirm the opinion advanced by Dr. Jenner' (Encyclopaedia Britannica, 7th ed., 1842).

items.bewering: Hy het die idee dus nie uitgedink nie, maar dit getoets en bekendgemaak.
items.bron: PMC3883152 and History News Network: the folk belief predates Jenner, and Benjamin Jesty used cowpox in 1774 but never published; Jenner's contribution was the tested and published demonstration. The careful framing is accurate.

items.bewering: Jenner se eie verslag is 'n primêre bron, want hy het die proewe self gedoen. Historici leer wat hy volgens sy eie verslag gedoen en gesien het. Dit bly sy eie weergawe, dus word dit teen ander bronne nagegaan.
items.blok: Hoe ons Jenner se storie ken
items.bron: University library guides (e.g. Southern Connecticut State University, UBC, Eastern Illinois University LibGuides on primary and secondary sources): first-hand accounts by participants are primary sources, and they are evidence to be read critically against other sources.

items.bewering: 'n Geskiedenisboek wat iemand anders later oor Jenner skryf, is 'n sekondêre bron.
items.blok: Hoe ons Jenner se storie ken
items.bron: University library guides (UMB, Nova Southeastern, EIU LibGuides): books that interpret or analyse primary material are secondary sources.

items.bewering: By inenting kry 'n mens 'n klein bietjie entstof wat na 'n siekte se kiem lyk. Die liggaam leer die kiem so ken voordat die siekte ooit kom. Die entstof help die liggaam dus om die siekte later te weerstaan.
items.bron: WHO, 'How do vaccines work?' (who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/how-do-vaccines-work): vaccines give the immune system harmless copies of an antigen, a part of the germ, so the body builds memory and responds faster when the real germ comes. The mapping holds: the vaccine resembles the germ, it does not cause the disease, and the body learns to recognise it in advance. In Jenner's case the look-alike was a related virus. A learner who takes it further and concludes that a vaccine resembles the germ is still right for the vaccines this lesson discusses.

items.bewering: Jenner se entstof was koeipokke en nie pokke self nie.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798), Case XVII: the material came from a cowpox sore. (Later genomic work suggests some 19th-century vaccine stocks were horsepox-like, but this concerns stocks after Jenner, not his 1796 material, and the lesson's sentence is right as written.)

items.bewering: Koeipokke is naverwant aan pokke, en daarom het dit teen pokke gehelp.
items.bron: PMC3136487 and Robert Koch Institute (edoc.rki.de/handle/176904/906): orthopoxviruses share many genetic and antigenic features, so infection with one gives substantial protection against the others. Jenner's observation that cowpox protected against smallpox is the classic example.

items.bewering: Die Latynse woord vir koei is 'vacca', en daarvan kom ons woord 'vaksinasie'.
items.bron: Etymonline, 'vaccination': from Latin vaccinus 'from cows', from vacca 'cow', tied to Jenner's cowpox technique (c. 1800). The Afrikaans 'vaksinasie' comes from the same word.

items.bewering: Inenting het pokke uiteindelik uit die wêreld gekry.
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox: the 1967 eradication programme, with widespread immunisation and surveillance, ended smallpox; the last natural case was in Somalia in 1977.

items.bewering: In 1980 het die Wêreldgesondheidsorganisasie verklaar dat pokke nêrens meer voorkom nie.
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox: 'In 1980 WHO declared smallpox eradicated'; World Health Assembly resolution WHA33.3, 8 May 1980.

items.bewering: Pokke is die enigste siekte van mense wat so uitgewis is.
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox: 'the only infectious disease to achieve this distinction'. Rinderpest was eradicated in 2011 but is a disease of animals, so the lesson's limit to 'siekte van mense' is the correct, careful form.

items.bewering: Pokke was 'n gevaarlike siekte wat dikwels merke op die vel gelaat het.
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox; CDC Museum, Smallpox (pitted scars on survivors).

items.bewering: Koeipokke is 'n siekte wat koeie en mense kan kry. Dit is naverwant aan pokke, maar baie minder gevaarlik.
items.bron: Jenner, Inquiry (1798) (cowpox in cows and in the people who milk them); PMC3136487 and RKI: human cowpox is usually a mild, self-limiting local infection and is an orthopoxvirus related to variola.

items.bewering: 'n Aansteeklike siekte versprei van een mens na 'n ander.
items.bron: WHO, Smallpox ('contagious disease') and standard usage: a contagious disease passes from person to person.

items.bewering: Inenting is wanneer 'n mens 'n entstof teen 'n siekte kry.
items.bron: WHO, 'How do vaccines work?'

items.bewering: 'n Middel wat 'n liggaam help om 'n bepaalde siekte later te weerstaan.
items.bron: WHO, 'How do vaccines work?' and WHO Europe, 'How vaccines work': each vaccine trains the body against a specific pathogen so it can resist it later.

items.bewering: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak. 'n Enkele kiem is te klein om met die blote oog te sien.
items.bron: KidsHealth (Nemours), 'Germs' (kidshealth.org/en/kids/germs.html), and Children's Minnesota, 'Germs: bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa': germs are tiny organisms, too small to see without a microscope, that can cause illness. Whether viruses such as smallpox count as 'living' is a known boundary question in biology. This is a school-level convention that is consistent across the subject, not a false statement.

items.bewering: 'n Bron is iets waaruit ons kan leer - 'n foto, 'n geskrif, 'n storie, 'n onderhoud of 'n voorwerp - oor nou of oor lank gelede.
items.bron: University library guides (UBC, SCSU LibGuides): historical sources include photographs, written documents, oral histories, interviews and artefacts.

items.bewering: 'n Bron wat van iemand kom wat self daar was: die mens self, of iemand wat dit gesien het. Dit bly 'n primêre bron, ook as sy dit jare later vertel.
items.bron: University library guides (Concordia, EIU, UMGC LibGuides): first-hand and eyewitness accounts are primary; memoirs, autobiographies and oral histories count as primary for the author's own experience even when recorded long afterwards.

items.bewering: 'n Bron waarin iemand wat nie self daar was nie, vertel of verklaar wat gebeur het deur op ander bronne te steun, soos 'n geskiedenisboek of 'n dokumentêr. Dit hang nie af van wanneer dit gemaak is nie.
items.bron: University library guides (UMB, Nova Southeastern LibGuides): secondary sources interpret or analyse primary material; history books and documentaries are typical examples. What makes them secondary is the distance from the event, not the date of making.

items.bewering: Historici is mense wat die geskiedenis ondersoek en daaroor skryf.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'historian': 'a person who studies or writes about history'; Merriam-Webster, 'historian'.

opsomming: All 34 checkable claims hold against sources, most of the Jenner details against his own 1798 Inquiry (two incisions, a boy of about eight, mild illness, later variolation, milkers off work for several days) and the eradication claims against WHO; both superlatives are correctly limited ('een van die', 'siekte van mense'), and the vaccine 'look-alike' comparison maps correctly.
